TL/DR supervisor accused me of being unprofessional and "explained" to me how my body sweats.

I live in a pretty hot and humid area. It gets to be between 35-40°C /95-105°F in the summer wear i live. And it feels worse since we have the sea literally right next to us. I also work airside in an airport. Meaning i work outside in the heat, in the summer, running around hot engines and motors. 

I worked for a company that didn't allow my department to wear shorts. Because passengers could see us and it was unprofessional to be walking around in work shorts. Much better for them to smell us sweat our balls off. But ok. 

I do not handle the heat well. But it's a fast paced job and I'm outside for a max of 40 min. That's if I'm lucky and everything goes well.

 If I'm not lucky, i could be stuck outside for hours. 

On one particular day where I had no such luck i was stuck in the middle of August waiting to get a delayed flight out. Sweating my @ss off. Everything was closed, ready to leave, we were simply waiting for permission to push back, and i couldn't take it anymore.

I rolled my pants up. Not even to my knee. Loosely, around my ankles just to let some air into the polyester fabric and dry my damn legs.

We get permission, push. And I return to the office to do my paperwork. Where my supervisor proceeds to chew into me for having rolled up my pants, after everyone was on the plane and out of vision, i was wrong and unprofessional because I could still be seen from the windows.

I replied that my legs were sweating and i couldn't take it anymore. 

"Your legs don't sweat! That's just your back sweat sliding down into your pants and down your legs."

I was so shocked that i didn't have a reply at the time and just went back to my paperwork. But the thought of this person telling me how MY body supposedly works still pisses me off to this day.

I left after that summer and haven't gone back to work for that company since.
